source_text: I. Apprehensi sunt adolescentes catechumini, Revocatus et Felicitas conserva ejus, Saturninus et Secundulus. Inter quos et Vivia Perpetua, honeste nata, liberaliter instituta, matronaliter nupta, habens patrem et matrem et fratres duos, alterum aeque catechuminum, et filium infantem ad ubera. Erat autem ipsa annorum circiter viginti duorum. Haec ordinem totum martyrii sui jam hinc ipsa narrabit, sicut conscriptum manu sua et suo sensu reliquit. II. « Cum adhuc, inquit, cum persecutoribus essemus, et me pater avertere et dejicere pro sua affectione perseveraret: Pater, inquio, vides, verbi gratia, vas hoc jacens, urceolum, sive aliud? » Et « dixit: Video. » Et ego dixi ei: « Numquid alio nomine vocari potest quam quod est? » Et ait: « Non. » « Sic et ego aliud me dicere non possum, nisi quod sum Christiana. » Tunc pater motus in hoc verbo, misit « se in me ut oculos mihi erueret: sed vexavit tantum, et profectus est victus cum argumentis diaboli, Tunc paucis diebus quod caruissem patre, Domino gratias egi, et refrigeravit absentia illius. In ipso spatio paucorum dierum baptizati sumus; mihi autem Spiritus dictavit nihil aliud petendum in aqua, nisi sufferentiam carnis. Post paucos dies recipimur in carcerem, et expavi, quia numquam experta eram tales tenebras. O diem asperum! aestus validos turbarum beneficio concussurae militum: novissime macerabar sollicitudine infantis. Ibi tunc Tertius et Pomponius, benedicti diacones, qui nobis ministrabant, constituerunt praemio ut, paucis horis emissi, in meliorem locum carceris refrigeraremus. Tunc exeuntes de carcere universi sibi vacabant. Ego infantem lactabam jam inedia defectum. Sollicita pro eo adloquebar matrem, et confortabam fratrem, commendabam filium. Tabescebam ideo quod illos tabescere videram mei beneficio. Tales sollicitudines multis diebus passa sum, et usurpavi ut mecum infans in carcere maneret; et statim convalui, et relevata sum a labore et sollicitudine infantis: et factus est mihi carcer subito quasi praetorium, ut ibi mallem esse quam alibi. « III. Tunc dixit mihi frater meus: Domina soror, jam in magna dignitate es; et tanta ut postules visionem, et ostendatur tibi an passio sit, an commeatus. Et ego, quae me sciebam fabulari cum Domino, cujus beneficia tanta experta eram, fidenter repromisi ei dicens: « Crastina die tibi renuntiabo. » Et postulavi, et ostensum est mihi hoc: Video scalam auream mirae magnitudinis pertingentem usque ad coelum et angustam, per quam non nisi singuli ascendere possent: et in lateribus scalae omne genus ferramentorum infixum. Erant ibi gladii, lanceae, hami, machaerae; ut si quis negligenter, aut non sursum adtendens ascenderet, laniaretur et carnes ejus inhaererent ferramentis. Et erat sub ipsa scala draco cubans mirae magnitudinis, qui ascendentibus insidias parabat, et exterrebat ne ascenderent. Ascendit autem Saturus prior, qui postea se propter nos ultro tradiderat, et tunc cum adducti sumus, praesens non fuerat: et pervenit in caput scalae, et convertit se ad me, et dixit mihi: « Perpetua, sustineo te. Sed vide ne te mordeat draco ille. » Et dixi ego: « Non me nocebit in nomine Domini Jesu Christi. » Et de sub ipsa scala quasi timens me, lente elevavit caput: et cum primum gradum calcassem, calcavi illius caput. Et ascendi et vidi spatium horti immensum, et in medio horti sedentem hominem canum, in habitu pastoris, grandem, oves mulgentem; et circumstantes candidati millia multa. Et levavit caput et adspexit me, et dixit mihi: « Bene venisti, tecnon. » Et clamavit me, et de caseo quod mulgebat dedit mihi quasi buccellam, et ego accepi junctis manibus, et manducavi: et universi circumstantes dixerunt, Amen. Et ad sonum vocis experrecta sum, commanducans adhuc dulcis nescio quid. Et retuli statim fratri meo, et intelleximus passionem esse futuram: et coepimus nullam jam spem in saeculo habere.

choices.english: in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ

pass_b_english: Young catechumens were seized: Revocatus and Felicity, her fellow slave, Saturninus and Secundulus. Among them was Vivia Perpetua, well-born, liberally educated, respectably married. She had a father and mother and two brothers, one of whom was also a catechumen, and an infant son at her breast. She was about twenty-two years old. She will now narrate the whole order of her martyrdom, as she left it written in her own hand and with her own understanding.

While we were still with the persecutors, my father kept trying to turn me away and cast me down out of his affection. "Father," I said, "you see, for example, this vessel lying here, a little jug, or something else?" He said, "I see." And I said to him, "Can it be called by any other name than what it is?" He said, "No." "Likewise I cannot call myself anything other than what I am, a Christian." Then my father, moved by this word, threw himself at me to gouge out my eyes; but he only annoyed me, and he went away defeated, along with the devil's arguments. After a few days without my father, I gave thanks to the Lord, and his absence refreshed me. In that same space of a few days we were baptized, and the Spirit dictated to me that I should ask for nothing else in the water except the endurance of the flesh. After a few days we were taken back to prison, and I was terrified, because I had never experienced such darkness. Oh harsh day! The fierce heat, the crush of the crowds, the soldiers' rough handling. Finally I was worn out with worry about my infant. There, Tertius and Pomponius, blessed deacons who were ministering to us, arranged for a fee that we might be released for a few hours to refresh ourselves in a better part of the prison. As we were leaving the prison, everyone took care of their own needs. I was nursing my infant, who was already failing from hunger. Anxious for him, I spoke to my mother, comforted my brother, commended my son. I was wasting away because I saw them wasting away for my sake. I suffered such anxieties for many days, and I managed to have my infant stay with me in prison; and immediately I recovered, and was relieved of the labor and worry of my infant. The prison suddenly became like a palace to me, so that I preferred to be there rather than anywhere else.

Then my brother said to me, "Lady sister, you are now in great dignity, and so great that you can ask for a vision, and it will be shown to you whether it is martyrdom or reprieve." I, who knew I was speaking with the Lord, whose great benefits I had experienced, confidently promised him, saying, "Tomorrow I will tell you." I asked, and this was shown to me: I see a golden ladder of amazing size reaching up to heaven, narrow, so that only one person could ascend at a time. On the sides of the ladder every kind of iron tool was fixed: swords, lances, hooks, daggers. If anyone ascended carelessly, or not looking upward, they would be torn and their flesh would stick to the iron tools. Under the ladder a dragon of amazing size lay crouching, preparing ambushes for those ascending, and frightening them so they would not ascend. But Saturus ascended first, who later handed himself over voluntarily on our behalf, and at that time, when we were led away, he was not present. He reached the top of the ladder, turned to me, and said, "Perpetua, I am waiting for you. But see that the dragon does not bite you." I said, "It will not harm me in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ." From under the ladder, as if fearing me, it slowly lifted its head. When I stepped on the first rung, I stepped on its head. I ascended and saw an immense garden space, and in the middle of the garden a grey-haired man sitting, dressed like a shepherd, large, milking sheep; and thousands of white-robed people standing around. He lifted his head, looked at me, and said, "You are welcome, child." He called me, and from the cheese he was milking gave me a morsel as if a little mouthful. I took it with joined hands and ate; and all those standing around said, "Amen." At the sound of the voice I woke up, still chewing something sweet. I immediately told my brother, and we understood that martyrdom was to come; and we began to have no hope in this world.
